title: Septic shock
banner: DRAFT, NOT clinically reviewed. Fictional scenario specification; never imported, published or shown to learners.
learning_objectives: Recognise possible sepsis in a deteriorating patient with suspected infection and escalate urgently.
Use a structured handover to the responsible clinical team.
Distinguish uninterrupted delivery through a safe line from immediate response to suspected vasopressor extravasation.
Recognise possible extravasation and act per protocol.

sources.use: NEWS2 report (2017): score-based clinical response, record the response, sepsis statements
FDA norepinephrine label: extravasation and abrupt discontinuation statements

Official 2026 SSC recommendation-level page: conditional, very-low-certainty preference for protocolized peripheral vasopressor initiation when central access would delay support; complete evidence tables not reviewed.

required_sources: Unit sepsis bundle and vasopressor protocol
Local adult vasopressor extravasation SOP including catheter aspiration, antidote and uninterrupted haemodynamic support
Full-text evidence tables for SSC 2026 and local/national sepsis pathway still require review
gaps: No published clinical scenario may exist until the review phase: this is a specification only.
The branching content, consequences and scoring are the author's reading of the cited sources and have had no clinical review.
Fluid choices, antimicrobial timing, lactate targets and blood-pressure targets are not drawn from a source read in full and are not written.
The NEWS2 statements are UK and 2017; the scenario names no score thresholds.

The steps are not a model-specific norepinephrine administration protocol. Local rules for catheter retention/aspiration, alternative venous access and antidote require critical care and pharmacy review.

Simulation option wording is synchronized with MD-01 and the vasopressor monitoring topic; do not treat synthetic debrief scoring as evidence of independent bedside competence. Clinician and pharmacist sign-off remain outstanding.
permissions: Cited sources are paraphrased only; see the licensing register for each source's reproduction status.
setting: A fictional adult with suspected pneumonia on a fictional unit.

steps.info: A patient with suspected pneumonia is more drowsy, feels hot and has a high early warning score on this set of observations.

options.text: Stay with the patient, assess airway, breathing and circulation, summon urgent clinical help for suspected sepsis, and use SBAR to convey findings and trends.
options.feedback: A new change in alertness with suspected infection warrants immediate assessment and urgent escalation. Sepsis and septic shock are emergencies; the SSC 2026 guidance calls for treatment and resuscitation without delay. NEWS2 supports recognition, but a score must not delay emergency help when clinical deterioration is apparent. Document the response after immediate safety needs are addressed.
options.consequence: The team attends promptly and the patient is reassessed.

options.text: Repeat the observations in an hour and see whether the score changes.
options.feedback: A high score is a trigger for an urgent response, not for waiting.
options.consequence: The patient deteriorates before the repeat is due.

options.text: Give a regular antipyretic and see whether the score settles.
options.feedback: Treating one sign does not address the cause and delays escalation.
options.consequence: The temperature falls but the underlying problem is unaddressed.

steps.info: The team starts a vasopressor infusion through a peripheral cannula as prescribed.
steps.prompt: What do you do while it runs?

options.text: Inspect the peripheral site and haemodynamics frequently under the unit protocol; report changes and avoid unplanned interruptions while the line is functioning.
options.feedback: The SSC 2026 recommendation allows peripheral vasopressor initiation for adult septic shock rather than delaying appropriate treatment for central access, with careful access surveillance and an extravasation response plan. Do not unnecessarily interrupt a working essential infusion. If the site becomes compromised, stop delivery at that cannula immediately while securing urgent alternative support through the local protocol.
options.consequence: The vascular access is monitored repeatedly, and the team has a plan for urgent alternative access if the site fails.

options.text: Check the site when the infusion is set up and not again.
options.feedback: Extravasation can happen at any time, so the site is monitored throughout.
options.consequence: A change at the site goes unnoticed.

options.text: Disconnect the infusion briefly to flush the line when it seems slow.
options.feedback: Interrupting a vasopressor can drop the pressure, and flushing changes drug delivery; this follows the protocol and the prescriber.
options.consequence: The pressure falls during the interruption.

steps.info: Later the skin over the cannula becomes pale, cool and swollen.

options.text: Suspect extravasation: stop delivery through the affected cannula now, call for help, and activate the unit's injury and alternative-access pathway.
options.feedback: Pallor, coolness or swelling at a norepinephrine catheter may indicate extravasation. Stop delivery through the affected cannula immediately; do not force-flush. Preserve the site/catheter for trained assessment under the local extravasation pathway, and urgently maintain patient perfusion via clinician-directed alternative access. Do not imply that all vasopressor treatment should be stopped.
options.consequence: The affected line is no longer infusing; trained staff assess the injury and organize alternative vasopressor access under the emergency protocol.

options.text: Slow the infusion and recheck in an hour.
options.feedback: Continuing possible vasopressor extravasation for another hour can worsen local tissue ischemia; stop delivery through the affected site and escalate without delay.

options.text: Massage the area to disperse the drug.
options.feedback: Do not massage or flush suspected vasopressor extravasation. Seek the trained team and follow the facility antidote/aspiration pathway.

learning_points: Assess airway, breathing and circulation and summon urgent help for suspected sepsis with deterioration; do not wait for a score. Communicate findings with structured handover.

Monitor peripheral vasopressor access during treatment. Suspected extravasation requires immediate cessation through the affected cannula, urgent escalation, and a plan for alternative vascular access and haemodynamic support.
Do not flush or massage suspected extravasation; manage the cannula and any antidote only under the appropriate trained-team/local protocol.
